AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
“In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability related modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the City Clerk’s office at 310-952-1720 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.” (Government Code Section 54954.2)

CALL TO ORDER: CITY COUNCIL

ROLL CALL:

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR MATTERS LISTED ON THE AGENDA (MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC) (LIMITED TO ONE HOUR) City Clerk read public comments from the following:

Liz Fiosia expressing concern of 
Jaime Monteclaro offering recommendations on how City Council can protect the public and provide service for city employees

Luna inquired about future ordinances related to the intentional spread of coronavirus and other diseases. 

Diane Faatai 


DISCUSSION: (Item 1)

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR MATTERS NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA (MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC)

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (COUNCIL MEMBERS)

ADJOURNMENT

1.. DISCUSSION AND ACTION ON MEASURES TO MITIGATE THE IMPACTS OF THE COVID-19 (CORONAVIRUS) PANDEMIC (CITY COUNCIL)  -  Action: adopted (Fail) City Manager Landers gave a brief staff report. 

Captain Skeen gave a report on crime trends related to COVID-19. In addition, he spoke about activation of EOC. 

Landers asked that Captain Skeen address unsafe parking 

Captain Skeen noted that (review tape) 

She also asked that he address EOC -

AR thanked Captain Skeen and Deputies for ensuring public safety. 

MPTJD inquired about how will the message get out about price gouging. In addition he requested clarity on the stay at home order. 

Captain Skeen clarified what can be done and not done during the stay at home order. He encouraged people to read Health and Safety Code 120295 as part of the Stay at home order. 

LDH commended Captain Skeen and thanked him for his efforts

Councilmember Hicks thanked Skeen and asked that he provide information for individuals requesting welfare checks. 

Captain Skeen noted people can call 310) 830-1123 or visit LASD website for those needing welfare checks. He thanked his deputies for being on the front line on behalf of the community. 

CM Landers noted the following: 
850 Active Employees
FTE 282 reduced by 19% - 54 employees was ask to go home and shelter in place. 
PTE 568 reduced by 86% - 470 employees were sent home. She noted that most of those effected were assigned to programs and parks that were suspended. 

AR asked CM Landers to address a rumor about custodial employees will be laid off. 

CM Landers clarified that no employees will be laid off as a result of the stay-home-order. 

Mike Whitaker gave information on the COVID-19 Task Force. Call Center 310) 952-1750. 

CM Landers thanked Mike Whitaker and his team for their efforts. 

AR thanked Mike Whitaker for his efforts. He directed staff to mail this information to every household by every door direct translated in Spanish and Tagalog.

JD noted to make sure the information that is disseminated is correct. 

LDH noted that Mike Whittaker worked in the City since he was 14 and applaud him for doing a fantastic job. 

JH commended Mike Whittaker

CH inquired about the limit on meals people can take. Mr. Whittaker noted that the number of people in the car are the number of meals they will received. and for those individuals that have seniors or children at home, no more then seven per car. 

LDH inquired about when the YMCA deliveries will begin. Mike noted the will begin on Thursday. and will be delivered Monday - Thursday. 

Asst CM Raymond gave a brief staff report on efforts made by Community Services and Public Works while delivering services to the community. 

CM Landers spoke about staff and city attorney efforts will be addressing price gouging business license revocations and 

JH made a motion to reverse the order and bring employees back to work, seconded by JD.

AR noted that the Health and Welfare of our employees are the most priority, making sure that each and every employee will be compensated at their full salary.  

LDH does not agree with the motion, she believe the city will make the employees whole in the event there is an issue. 

JD inquired about the States time (review tape) In addition, he noted that he received a letter from union president stated opposite from what the mayor is saying. He requested that the union president be brought in on the call. 

Discussion ensued about the city's intentions on making employees heard. 


motion failed for lack of majority vote.

JD spoke about the decision to suspend the city's bus service. He also inquired about the status of the City's effort on the city's of carson becoming a test center. 

Discussion ensued about the importance of suspending the bus service. 
CM Landers noted that a letter was sent to (governor)? review tape - In addition JD asked if there is any progress with Victoria Park becoming a emergency mobile hospital. 

JD also inquired about if the city could partner with food services through (Dr. Philippine doctor). 

He asked about city employees wanting to volunteer. CM noted that city employees will be calling people back as the need arise, in lieu of using volunteers. 

LDH requested that a letter be mailed to commercial property owners requesting that some sort of reprieve be giving to their tenants as it relates to rents and evictions. 

In addition she inquired about how staff are to move forward with upcoming city events. 

Mayor Robles directed staff to place an item on the agenda to discuss city events, in addition to an item to discuss moratorium on commercial property and rents. 

CH directed staff to look into Small Business Loan opportunities to provide to the small business community.

CH inquired if the city is tracking (review tape) - and loss revenue at the Community Center. 
 
CM Landers noted that she is working with Captain Skeen in tracking that information. In addtion, she noted that Finance Director Rahmani will be looking into additional revenue sources and will have loss of revenue. 

He also asked how is the city tracking the whereabouts of the individuals testing positive of the COVID-19. CM Landers noted that city staff have now way of finding out where those individuals live or have traveled too throughout the city. She noted the Department of Public Health is tracking that information citing HIPPA laws. 

Discussion ensued about the local Farmers Market. 

AR concluded noted that city council is unanimous about the health and safety of residents, employees and business is the priority. These are difficult unprecedented times.

JD would like to add to the agenda a briefing of Waste Basin Rep, Harold Williams. 

AR
